Understanding authentication is crucial: Understanding authentication is crucial for protecting your application's data. This page will guide you through what mbc-cqrs-serverless features to use to implement auth.

Decides what routes and data the user ca: Decides what routes and data the user can access.

Once a user is authenticated, you can implement authorization to control what the user can access and do within your application. Authorization is orthogonal and independent from authentication. However, authorization requires an authentication mechanism.

`RolesGuard` resolves a user's effective: `RolesGuard` resolves a user's effective roles in two steps:
**Direct roles** — read from the JWT `cu: **Direct roles** — read from the JWT `custom:roles` claim for the active tenant.
**Group-derived roles** — if the direct: **Group-derived roles** — if the direct roles do not satisfy the required roles, the guard resolves roles from the user's groups listed in the `custom:groups` claim (tenant-scoped).
The mapping from a group to its roles is: The mapping from a group to its roles is **not** stored in the JWT. Your application provides it by implementing a resolver.

Implement exactly **one** resolver per a: Implement exactly **one** resolver per application and register it in your module `providers`. `AuthModule` is imported automatically via `AppModule.forRoot()`.
Do not add @Injectable() — @GroupRoleRes: Do not add @Injectable() — @GroupRoleResolver() already registers a singleton provider

**Singleton only** — the resolver is res: **Singleton only** — the resolver is resolved once at bootstrap; do not use `REQUEST`/`TRANSIENT` scope. Adding `@Injectable()` on the same class can override the scope and break bootstrap.
**Let failures propagate** — a resolver: **Let failures propagate** — a resolver error surfaces as a 5xx, not a silent 403, so a backend outage is distinguishable from a genuine access denial. Do not catch-and-grant.
**Case-sensitive roles** — keep the role: **Case-sensitive roles** — keep the role casing in `custom:roles` consistent with your `@Roles(...)` values.

Authorization attributes such as `custom:roles`, `custom:tenant` and `custom:groups` must be managed server-side with `AdminUpdateUserAttributes` after checking the caller's permission.
Before v1.8.1, the CLI template omitted: Before v1.8.1, the CLI template omitted `writeAttributes`. Signed-in users could update authorization attributes with their own access token, granting themselves roles, changing tenant or joining privileged groups. The fix changes the template only: existing projects must edit and deploy their own stack, review frontend writes and audit all users. Upgrading packages alone is insufficient.

By default, the JWT `custom:tenant` take: By default, the JWT `custom:tenant` takes priority over `x-tenant-code`. Set `EXPLICIT_TENANT_SELECTION_CODES=common` to allow eligible callers to explicitly select `common`; use `common,*` to include other nonempty tenant codes. The setting defaults to empty (disabled) and is read at request time.
Selection requires a nonempty direct `cu: Selection requires a nonempty direct `custom:roles` role for the target tenant, or `system_admin` in any tenant or global entry. Group membership alone and an unrelated global `admin` role do not qualify the caller. Route role checks still apply after tenant selection.
For an eligible explicit selection, `ten: For an eligible explicit selection, `tenantCode`, `tenantRole`, `tenantRoles` and `tenantGroupIds` refer to the selected tenant. Only that tenant's direct roles and group IDs are used; unrelated global roles such as `admin` are not inherited. A `system_admin` entry from any scope is preserved in `tenantRoles` and takes priority in `tenantRole`. The group resolver receives the selected tenant and its groups.
Configuration entries are comma-separate: Configuration entries are comma-separated, trimmed, case-insensitive and deduplicated; empty entries are ignored. Opted-in header values and matching role/group tenant codes are trimmed and lowercased. Headers outside the opt-in list keep legacy normalization.
Select the header tenant, even when the: Select the header tenant, even when the JWT home differs
Keep the JWT home; without a home, resol: Keep the JWT home; without a home, resolve no tenant
Resolve no tenant and deny; never fall b: Resolve no tenant and deny; never fall back to the home
Missing, empty or whitespace header whil: Missing, empty or whitespace header while enabled
Keep the home; without a home, deny: Keep the home; without a home, deny
Named entries take precedence over `*`,: Named entries take precedence over `*`, regardless of configuration order. Therefore `common,*` preserves the named `common` compatibility fallback, while `*` alone treats `common` as a wildcard target and requires eligibility. `RolesGuard` denies unresolved tenants even on routes with no role metadata.
Deploy clients that omit `x-tenant-code`: Deploy clients that omit `x-tenant-code` when no tenant is selected before enabling the setting. For an eligible caller, any opted-in header is an explicit choice, including a previously hard-coded `common` header. A home admin with a target user role receives only the target user permissions; a home user with a target admin role receives the target admin permissions.
This opt-in is independent of `COMMON_TE: This opt-in is independent of `COMMON_TENANT_CODES` (default `common`) and `CROSS_TENANT_ROLES` (default `system_admin`); their defaults are unchanged. Custom guards and package policies still apply. In particular, the master package's optional access policy can independently reject no-home access to a non-common tenant even when core accepts the selection.

Use the core `getUserContext()` helper s: Use the core `getUserContext()` helper so guards and services share tenant selection and scoped role/group resolution. By default the JWT home tenant wins; the explicit selection opt-in is described below.
When extending tenant verification, pres: When extending tenant verification, preserve `super.verifyTenant(context)` and add application checks after it. Do not replace core tenant resolution with a helper that always trusts a header.
Accepts validated explicit selections; o: Accepts validated explicit selections; otherwise uses the legacy common-tenant or cross-tenant-role policy
With explicit selection disabled, a JWT: With explicit selection disabled, a JWT home tenant keeps priority over the header. When explicit selection is enabled, core first validates direct membership or `system_admin` authority for the selected target; [the rules above](/docs/authentication#explicit-tenant-selection) apply.
